headline.purpose: The login screen's title — the only page-level headline in the app.

title.purpose: Section and modal headers (panel headers, chat header, modal titles).

subtitle.purpose: Login subtext, form inputs, and compact section sub-headers (calendar/list panel titles, Excel section headings).

body.purpose: Default UI text — buttons, list rows, message text.

label.purpose: Emphasized micro-text — table column headers, admin sub-group headings.

caption.purpose: The smallest tier — badge text, meta/timestamp lines, calendar weekday labels.

shadows.name: floating-panel
shadows.purpose: Reaction picker and @-mention autocomplete dropdown — the only resting-shadow surfaces in the system.

shadows.name: modal-scrim
shadows.purpose: Full-viewport dimming background behind a modal; the modal card itself stays flat/bordered, not shadowed.

shadows.name: sidebar-scrim
shadows.purpose: Lighter backdrop behind the off-canvas sidebar drawer below 1024px — a navigation surface, not an interrupting one, so it dims less than the modal scrim.

motion.name: standard-ease
motion.purpose: The single transition timing used everywhere: toggle switch, sidebar slide-in, toast enter/exit.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The reusable primary button — currently just "+ 방 만들기" (create room). Same compact footprint as secondary/danger/ghost, never stretched to fill its container. The only button variant with a hover state in the whole system.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-text); border: none; border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 12px; font-weight: 600; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", "Malgun Gothic", sans-serif; font-size: 13px; cursor: pointer; align-self: flex-start; transition: background-color 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--primary-hover); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default button for most actions (create room, save, add).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 12px; font-family: inherit; font-size: 13px; cursor: pointer; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive actions only — delete room/message/user, demote admin. Uses the fill-role token (Alert Coral Fill), not the text-role Alert Coral token, since white text sits on top of it.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: var(--danger-fill); color: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--danger-fill); border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 12px; font-family: inherit; font-size: 13px; cursor: pointer; }

components.name: Unread Count Badge
components.description: Per-room and sidebar unread-message counter. Inverts to white-bg/coral-text when placed on the already-blue active nav link. Uses the fill-role token (Alert Coral Fill).
components.css: .ds-badge-count { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 18px; height: 18px; padding: 0 5px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--danger-fill); color: #fff; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: Message-level and file-affordance actions (react, view reactors, delete a message, attach a file, drag-and-drop overlay) — inline Feather-style SVG, stroke=currentColor so it inherits the button's own color/hover state, plus a Korean title/aria-label. Replaces raw emoji glyphs (🙂+/🗑/👥/📎) that carried no real affordance and often no accessible label at all. The theme toggle (🌙/☀️), room-visibility (🔒/🔓), and the reaction picker's emoji are deliberately unaffected — those emoji carry real-world or content meaning, not UI-chrome.
components.html: <button type="button" class="ds-icon-btn" title="메시지 삭제" aria-label="메시지 삭제"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="14" height="14" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polyline points="3 6 5 6 21 6"/><path d="M19 6v14a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H7a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V6m3 0V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h4a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v2"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-icon-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 2px; background: transparent; border: none; color: var(--text-muted); cursor: pointer; } .ds-icon-btn:hover { opacity: 0.7; }

components.name: Toast
components.description: Non-blocking, self-dismissing status notice (showToast(text)). Originally for mention notifications, now the default for any transient status the app needs to tell the user (reaction/delete/upload errors, room-membership/deletion notices) — replacing what used to be alert(). A couple of call sites that redirect right after showing one delay the navigation by ~1.5s so the toast is actually readable, since unlike alert() it doesn't block.
components.css: .ds-toast { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 14px; font-size: 13px; color: var(--text); box-shadow: 0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.18); transition: opacity 0.2s ease, transform 0.2s ease; }

components.name: Selection Modal
components.description: Themed modal for picking one person from a list and acting on them (초대할 사용자 선택 in 참여 인원; 새 방장 in 방장 위임) — replaces a native prompt(). Same modal chrome as Confirm Modal, with a single native <select> as the body instead of a message.
components.html: 방장 위임
components.css: .ds-modal-overlay { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; } .ds-modal { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px; width: 100%; max-width: 560px; padding: 20px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }

components.name: Broken Image Fallback
components.description: Swapped in for an image message's on load failure (404, corrupt file, network error), instead of leaving the browser's own broken-image icon exposed. Fixed 180x120px, dashed border, centered broken-image icon + "이미지를 불러올 수 없습니다" text.
components.html: 이미지를 불러올 수 없습니다
components.css: .ds-msg-image-fallback { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; width: 180px; height: 120px; border: 1px dashed var(--border); border-radius: 8px; color: var(--text-muted); font-size: 12px; }

components.name: Reaction Pill
components.description: Emoji reaction count under a chat message. Highlights amber/bold when the current user is one of the reactors.
components.css: .ds-reaction-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); font-size: 12px; cursor: pointer; line-height: 1.6; } .ds-reaction-pill:hover { border-color: var(--primary); } .ds-reaction-pill.ds-mine { background: var(--mention-bg); border-color: var(--primary); font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Own Message Bubble
components.description: The current user's own chat message, right-aligned with the primary fill.
components.css: .ds-msg-bubble-mine { max-width: 70%; margin-left: auto; background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-text); border-radius: 12px; padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 13px; word-break: break-word; white-space: pre-wrap; }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Link
components.description: App-shell navigation row. Active state fills solid primary with a text-colored left accent bar — the only left-border accent in the system.
components.css: .ds-sidebar-link { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-left: 3px solid transparent; background: var(--bg); color: var(--text-muted); font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; text-decoration: none; } .ds-sidebar-link.ds-active { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-text); border-color: var(--primary); border-left-color: var(--text); } .ds-sidebar-link.ds-active .ds-badge-count { background: #fff; color: var(--danger-fill); }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Standard text/select/textarea styling. No custom focus ring exists in the source — falls back to the browser default outline.
components.css: .ds-input { padding: 8px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); font-family: inherit; font-size: 13px; }

components.name: Panel / Card
components.description: The base container for room lists, the schedule calendar, and other grouped content. Flat — border only, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px; padding: 16px; }

components.name: Confirm Modal
components.description: Shared themed confirmation for every destructive action (delete room/message/user/issue/schedule, demote/promote admin), replacing native confirm() — the desktop (Electron) build was found to leave input dead after a native dialog closes. A generic app-wide Escape handler (modal-escape.js) now also closes any other visible .modal-overlay by delegating to its own .modal-close button, so every modal in the system — not just this one — closes on Escape.

narrative.overview:
TeamChat reads like a tool people duck into mid-task, not a product they spend time in. Everything about it — the flat gray panels, the single blue accent reserved for one action per screen, the system font stack with a Korean fallback baked in — says internal utility over showcase. It is calm and unapologetically plain: no illustration, no marketing chrome, no attempt to feel like a consumer chat app. The restraint isn't cold, though — rounded corners on nearly everything (8–12px, going fully pill-shaped for anything that's a count or a tag), a small set of semantic emoji kept where the glyph itself carries real-world meaning (🌙/☀️ for theme, 🔒/🔓 for room visibility, 🟢/⚪ for online status), minimal stroke-style SVG icons for message-level and file actions, and a warm amber highlight for mentions keep it from reading as sterile. The overall character the team confirmed: restrained, but warm.

The system is fully dark-mode mirrored via a data-theme attribute the user toggles explicitly (falling back to prefers-color-scheme when unset) — every token has a light and dark value, and both are load-bearing, not an afterthought.
keyCharacteristics: One accent color (signal-blue) used sparingly, for the single primary action on a screen — not scattered across secondary buttons.
Flat by default: every resting surface (panel, card, button, input) is bordered, not shadowed.
Elevation is reserved for floating/transient layers only (pickers, dropdowns, modal scrims).
Pill shape (999px) marks anything representing a count, status, or tag; 8–10px marks containers and controls.
Full light/dark parity — no color exists in only one theme.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue appears on at most one control per screen — the primary action. Secondary, danger, and ghost buttons all stay neutral; adding blue to more than the single primary action breaks the system's restraint.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface's edge is drawn with a 1px border in the neutral border color, never a shadow. Shadows are reserved for floating layers only.

rules.name: The Two-Weight Rule
rules.body: Text is either regular body weight or bumped to 600–700 for emphasis (names, titles, badges) — there is no intermediate 500 weight anywhere in the system.

rules.name: The Grounded-Except-Floating Rule
rules.body: If it sits in the document flow, it's flat and bordered. If it floats above the page (picker, dropdown, scrim), it gets a shadow. Nothing in between.

rules.name: The Text-vs-Fill Rule
rules.body: Any signal color used both as text-on-neutral-bg and as a fill-carrying-white-text needs two tokens, not one — the two roles pull lightness in opposite directions in dark mode. Alert Coral / Alert Coral Fill is the concrete instance; apply the same split before reusing a signal color in a new fill context.

dos: Do keep Signal Blue on exactly one control per screen (The One Accent Rule) — don't reach for it as a general "important button" color.
Do draw every surface edge with the shared 1px neutral border, not a shadow.
Do reserve box-shadow for floating/transient layers (pickers, dropdowns, the modal scrim) — never on a resting card, panel, or button.
Do add any new color to both the light and dark theme blocks together; this system has no color that exists in only one mode.
Do use the full pill radius (999px) for anything that represents a count, status, or tag, and 8–10px for containers/controls.
Do theme scrollbars (and any other browser-default surface — focus rings, selection color) from the existing palette rather than leaving them unstyled or inventing a new color for them.
donts: Don't add hover or focus-visible styling to a button, panel, or list row and assume it matches an existing pattern — most of the system has none; only reaction pills, table rows, calendar cells, the mention-autocomplete list, and .btn-primary currently define hover feedback.

Don't introduce a second brand/accent color for a new feature. The palette is deliberately one action color plus role-bound signal colors (danger, mention, and the two schedule categories) — a new feature should reuse one of these roles, not add a new hue.
Don't give English marketing copy or decorative illustration a home here — every string in the product is Korean, and the tone is internal-tool plain, not promotional.
Don't size a widget for the standalone page it used to be once it's embedded in the shared rooms dashboard — widgets sharing that grid should stay compact enough that every region stays usable.

Don't use a native confirm(), prompt(), or alert() anywhere — use window.confirmDialog(message) for a yes/no decision, showToast(text) for a status notice, and a themed modal + select for picking from a list. The native dialogs are the known cause of dead renderer input in the desktop build.
